newsitem.title: USA: FIGURE SKATING-PUNSALAN/SWALLOW WIN DANCE AT U.S. CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-PUNSALAN/SWALLOW WIN DANCE AT U.S. CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Elizabeth Punsalan and Jerod Swallow won their fourth U.S. Figure Skating Championships dance title Thursday.

Receiving unanimous first-place ordinals, the couple, who placed seventh in the 1996 world championships, skated a cha-cha progam that was almost flawless expect for a brief fall during the first minute.
Last year's bronze medallists Eve Chalom and Matthew Gates won the silver medal and Kate Robinson and Peter Breen finished third.
"The fourth title is significant for us," Swallow said. "We really want to step up our speed and flow for worlds."
Punsalan and Swallow skated to a Latin medley that included twisting lifts and frenetically paced but controlled footwork.
Chalom and Gates followed with their own Latin medley. "We have a feel for it," Chalom said. "We like to get the crowd involved."
Robinson and Breen skated to Irish clogging music.
Also in competition Thursday night at the Nashville Arena, Todd Eldredge skated a near flawless programme to earn nine first-place ordinals and win the men's short programme.
Damon Allen, who finished third at the Vienna Cup in 1996 and fourth at the Trophy de France in 1995, took second place and former 1994 national champion Scott Davis stood in third.
"I'm on a high tonight," Allen said. "This is my first time in the medal standings."
Eldredge was the expected leader, and viewed his win without much emotion.
His coach, Richard Callaghan, said Eldredge had been skating with much more confidence since winning the world title last March.
"It has a lot to do with training every day," he said. "My confidence is up more knowing everything is going well."
The short programme counts for just a third of the men's final total. The long programme will decide the United States world team on Saturday.
